name: Battle of Marchfeld, Habsburg Defeats Bohemia
summary: Rudolf of Habsburg defeats and kills Ottokar II of Bohemia at the Battle of Marchfeld (Dürnkrut), the largest cavalry battle of the 13th century. Ottokar had built a central European empire stretching from Silesia to the Adriatic; his death allows Rudolf to grant Austria, Styria, and Carinthia to his sons, establishing the Habsburg territorial base. Rudolf's victory also demonstrates that imperial authority could check over-mighty princes.

_quarry.structural_significance: Marchfeld is the foundation moment of Habsburg power, the territorial base acquired here supports Habsburg imperial ambitions for centuries; Ottokar's empire, had it survived, might have created a Bohemian-Austrian power that could have resisted both Hungarians and Ottomans; the battle's outcome shapes central European political geography by establishing Habsburgs in Austria rather than the more historically natural Bohemian-Premyslid control
